rationale:
The supplied EG92-style proof of WhitneyExtension splits into two independent halves, and each half is a reusable lemma in its own right.

(1) whitney_smooth_partition_of_unity covers parent steps 0-3 plus (F4). It is a geometric Whitney partition of unity on U = ℝⁿ∖A for any closed nonempty A and does not involve h or ν. Its conclusion is seven properties (P1)-(P7):
- every anchor p_i lies in A;
- every φ_i is C¹ off A, nonnegative, and the family is locally finite with sum 1;
- wherever φ_i(x) ≠ 0, the anchor satisfies |x − p_i| ≤ C·d(x);
- Σ‖Dφ_i‖ ≤ M/d wherever d ≤ 1.

(2) whitney_jet_gluing_c1 covers parent steps 4-6. Take any family with exactly those properties, and any g with g = h on A and g equal to the averaged first-order Taylor formula Σᶠ φ_i·(h(p_i) + ⟨ν(p_i), · − p_i⟩) off A. Then g is C¹ and Dg(x)v = ⟨ν(x), v⟩ on A.
- The conclusion is about this pinned-down g, so the lemma cannot be discharged by some unrelated construction.
- Its hypotheses are verbatim the conjuncts of child (1).
- It drops the unused hypothesis ContinuousOn h A, which only makes it stronger.

Parent proof after the split: if A = ∅, take g = 0. Otherwise obtain (ι, φ, p, C, M) from (1), define g by classical cases, and apply (2). There are no sibling dependencies.

Evidence, all run in a scratch copy:
- Both one-line types pass lean_contract.validate_lean_statement.
- Both elaborate in the NodeChallenge modules generated by gmt-compare.py's own child_modules (import GMT.Ch02.Submission plus the replayed contract scope), against a scratch olean of the frozen Submission.
- `theorem assembly_check (c1 : <type 1>) (c2 : <type 2>) : WhitneyExtension` kernel-checks; its only axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
- Child (1)'s exact type was proved in Lean from a non-module port of the pinned SimonGMT WhitneyCover/Jet/Partition/Extension sources, with C = 2 and M = 100·M₀, using the same three axioms only.
- An independent adversarial reviewer checked:
  - truth, including A = ∅, A = univ, n = 0 and the finsum/fderiv conventions;
  - sufficiency of the two children for the parent;
  - every constant;
  - faithfulness to the supplied proof.
  The verdict was ACCEPT. Both of its minor remark fixes are incorporated: the list of files to port, and restricting the anchor bound to indices with φ_i(x) ≠ 0.

Why split rather than keep one node:
- The formal content is large; the SimonGMT reference implementation is about 1200 lines.
- The two halves are independent, so they can be proved in parallel.
- In the shared package tree the SimonGMT Whitney .oleans are stale for Lake, and WhitneyExtension has no .olean at all. Workers must port source either way, and the split halves that work per worker and keeps a failure local to one half.

The node is at depth 1, below the limit of 6. Child (2) may split further in its own session, for example into the first-order estimate and the continuity of the derivative.

subproblems.title: Whitney partition of unity on the complement of a closed set
subproblems.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ and every closed nonempty A ⊆ ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), writing d(x) := dist(x, A) (Metric.infDist x A), there exist a type ι, functions φ_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ and points p_i ∈ ℝⁿ (i ∈ ι), and real numbers C ≥ 0, M ≥ 0 such that: (P1) p_i ∈ A for every i; (P2) every φ_i is C¹ at every point x ∉ A; (P3) φ_i(x) ≥ 0 for every i and every x ∉ A; (P4) every x ∉ A has a neighbourhood V and a finite set s ⊆ ι with φ_i(y) = 0 for all i ∉ s and y ∈ V; (P5) Σᶠ_i φ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∉ A; (P6) for x ∉ A, φ_i(x) ≠ 0 implies |x − p_i| ≤ C·d(x); (P7) for x ∉ A with d(x) ≤ 1, Σᶠ_i ‖Dφ_i(x)‖ ≤ M/d(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Set (Rn n)), IsClosed A → A.Nonempty → ∃ (ι : Type) (φ : ι → Rn n → ℝ) (p : ι → Rn n) (C M : ℝ), 0 ≤ C ∧ 0 ≤ M ∧ (∀ i, p i ∈ A) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ x ∉ A, ContDiffAt ℝ 1 (φ i) x) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ x ∉ A, 0 ≤ φ i x) ∧ (∀ x ∉ A, ∃ s : Finset ι, ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 x, ∀ i ∉ s, ∀ y ∈ V, φ i y = 0) ∧ (∀ x ∉ A, ∑ᶠ i, φ i x = 1) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ x ∉ A, φ i x ≠ 0 → ‖x - p i‖ ≤ C * Metric.infDist x A) ∧ (∀ x ∉ A, Metric.infDist x A ≤ 1 → ∑ᶠ i, ‖fderiv ℝ (φ i) x‖ ≤ M / Metric.infDist x A)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: this is steps 0-3 and fact (F4) of the parent-supplied proof of WhitneyExtension (Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6, proof supplied after [EG92], Whitney's extension theorem), extracted as a stand-alone lemma. Notation: ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Euclidean norm |·|; ‖·‖ is the operator norm of a linear functional; B(x,ρ) and B̄(x,ρ) are the open and closed balls; U := ℝⁿ∖A; d(x) := dist(x, A) = Metric.infDist x A.

Claim. Let A ⊆ ℝⁿ be closed and nonempty. There are a type ι, functions φ_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ, points p_i ∈ ℝⁿ (i ∈ ι) and reals C ≥ 0, M ≥ 0 with
(P1) p_i ∈ A for every i;
(P2) every φ_i is C¹ at every point of U (ContDiffAt ℝ 1);
(P3) φ_i(x) ≥ 0 for every i and x ∈ U;
(P4) every x ∈ U has a neighbourhood V and a finite set s ⊆ ι with φ_i ≡ 0 on V for all i ∉ s;
(P5) Σᶠ_i φ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∈ U;
(P6) if x ∈ U and φ_i(x) ≠ 0, then |x − p_i| ≤ C·d(x);
(P7) if x ∈ U and d(x) ≤ 1, then Σᶠ_i ‖Dφ_i(x)‖ ≤ M/d(x).

Proof.

1. Distance and scale. Because A is closed and nonempty: d is 1-Lipschitz; d(x) ≤ |x − a| for a ∈ A (infDist_le_dist_of_mem); d(x) > 0 exactly for x ∈ U (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos); and, ℝⁿ being proper, every y ∈ ℝⁿ has a nearest point a ∈ A with |y − a| = d(y) (IsClosed.exists_infDist_eq_dist). U is open. Put r(x) := min{1, d(x)}/20. Then 0 ≤ r(x) ≤ 1/20, r(x) ≤ d(x)/20, r(x) > 0 for x ∈ U, r(x) = d(x)/20 whenever d(x) ≤ 1, and |r(x) − r(y)| ≤ |x − y|/20 for all x, y (t ↦ min{1,t} is 1-Lipschitz). For n = 0 the space is a single point, so A = ℝ⁰ and U = ∅; then the construction below produces the empty family and (P1)-(P7) hold vacuously (with C = 3, M as below).

2. Covering. Apply the Vitali covering lemma (Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall with index set U, centres x ↦ x, radii r, bound R := 1/20 and τ := 5 > 3). It gives J ⊆ U such that the closed balls B̄(s, r(s)), s ∈ J, are pairwise disjoint and every x ∈ U has some s ∈ J with B̄(x, r(x)) ⊆ B̄(s, 5r(s)); in particular |x − s| ≤ 5r(s). Write r_s := r(s); r_s > 0 because s ∈ U. (If U = ∅ then J = ∅.)

3. (F1) Comparable radii. Let s ∈ J and |x − s| ≤ 10r_s. Then |r(x) − r_s| ≤ |x − s|/20 ≤ r_s/2, so r_s/2 ≤ r(x) ≤ 3r_s/2, i.e. (2/3)r(x) ≤ r_s ≤ 2r(x). Moreover d(s) ≥ 20r_s (since r_s ≤ d(s)/20), so d(x) ≥ d(s) − |x − s| ≥ 10r_s > 0 and x ∈ U.

4. (F2) Bounded overlap. For x ∈ U let J(x) := {s ∈ J : |x − s| < 10r_s}. Claim: J(x) is finite and #J(x) ≤ N, where N := 33ⁿ depends only on n. For s ∈ J(x), (F1) gives r_s ≥ (2/3)r(x) and r_s ≤ 2r(x), so B̄(s, r_s) ⊆ B̄(x, |x − s| + r_s) ⊆ B̄(x, 11r_s) ⊆ B̄(x, 22r(x)). These closed balls are pairwise disjoint and each has Lebesgue measure at least the measure of a ball of radius (2/3)r(x) > 0. Hence for every finite F ⊆ J(x), comparing Lebesgue measures (measure of a ball of radius ρ = ρⁿ × measure of the unit ball), #F·((2/3)r(x))ⁿ ≤ (22r(x))ⁿ, i.e. #F ≤ 33ⁿ. Therefore J(x) is finite with #J(x) ≤ 33ⁿ. (Equivalently: distinct s, t ∈ J(x) satisfy |s − t| > r_s + r_t ≥ (4/3)r(x) by disjointness, so the rescaled points (s − x)/r(x), s ∈ J(x), form a (4/3)-separated subset of the fixed compact ball B̄(0, 20); a separated subset of a fixed compact set has cardinality bounded by a constant depending only on n. Any such uniform N may be used below.)

5. (F3) Local finiteness. For x₀ ∈ U let J'(x₀) := {s ∈ J : B(s, 10r_s) ∩ B(x₀, r(x₀)) ≠ ∅}. Then J(x) ⊆ J'(x₀) for every x ∈ B(x₀, r(x₀)) (x lies in both balls), and J'(x₀) is finite: if z ∈ B(s, 10r_s) ∩ B(x₀, r(x₀)), then (F1) at z gives (2/3)r(z) ≤ r_s ≤ 2r(z), while |r(z) − r(x₀)| ≤ |z − x₀|/20 < r(x₀)/20; hence r_s ≥ (2/3)(19/20)r(x₀) ≥ r(x₀)/2 and r_s ≤ 2(21/20)r(x₀) < 3r(x₀). So |s − x₀| ≤ |s − z| + |z − x₀| < 10r_s + r(x₀) < 31r(x₀) and B̄(s, r_s) ⊆ B̄(x₀, 34r(x₀)). These are pairwise disjoint balls of radius ≥ r(x₀)/2 > 0 inside B̄(x₀, 34r(x₀)), so by the measure comparison of step 4 there are at most 68ⁿ of them.

6. (F4) Anchors. For each s ∈ J fix a_s ∈ A with |s − a_s| = d(s) (step 1). If x ∈ U and s ∈ J(x), then |x − a_s| < 3d(x). Indeed d(s) ≤ d(x) + |x − s|, so |a_s − x| ≤ |a_s − s| + |s − x| = d(s) + |s − x| ≤ d(x) + 2|s − x| < d(x) + 20r_s ≤ d(x) + 40r(x) ≤ 3d(x), using r_s ≤ 2r(x) from (F1) and r(x) ≤ d(x)/20.

7. Rescaled bumps. Fix a C^∞ function θ : ℝⁿ → ℝ with 0 ≤ θ ≤ 1, θ = 1 on B̄(0,5) and θ(y) = 0 whenever |y| ≥ 9 (Mathlib: the ContDiffBump centred at 0 with rIn = 5, rOut = 9, whose support is B(0,9)). θ is C¹ with compact support, hence Lipschitz with some constant Λ ≥ 0 (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport). For s ∈ J let θ_s(x) := θ((x − s)/r_s). Then θ_s is C^∞ on ℝⁿ, 0 ≤ θ_s ≤ 1, θ_s(x) = 1 if |x − s| ≤ 5r_s, θ_s(x) ≠ 0 implies |x − s| < 9r_s, and θ_s is (Λ/r_s)-Lipschitz, so ‖Dθ_s(x)‖ ≤ Λ/r_s for all x (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz). Two vanishing properties:
(7a) If x ∈ U and s ∈ J ∖ J(x), i.e. |x − s| ≥ 10r_s, then θ_s ≡ 0 on B(x, r_s), because |y − x| < r_s gives |y − s| > 9r_s; hence Dθ_s(x) = 0.
(7b) If x₀ ∈ U, s ∈ J ∖ J'(x₀) and y ∈ B(x₀, r(x₀)), then θ_s(y) = 0; otherwise |y − s| < 9r_s and y ∈ B(s, 10r_s) ∩ B(x₀, r(x₀)), i.e. s ∈ J'(x₀).

8. Normalising sum. Let Σ(x) := Σᶠ_{s∈J} θ_s(x). Fix x₀ ∈ U and put F := J'(x₀) (finite by step 5). By (7b), Σ(y) = Σ_{s∈F} θ_s(y) for all y ∈ B(x₀, r(x₀)), which is a neighbourhood of x₀. Hence Σ is C^∞ at x₀ and DΣ(x₀) = Σ_{s∈F} Dθ_s(x₀) = Σ_{s∈J(x₀)} Dθ_s(x₀) (by (7a), since J(x₀) ⊆ F). Using r_s ≥ (2/3)r(x₀) for s ∈ J(x₀) (F1) and #J(x₀) ≤ N (F2): ‖DΣ(x₀)‖ ≤ Σ_{s∈J(x₀)} Λ/r_s ≤ (3/2)NΛ/r(x₀). Moreover Σ(x₀) ≥ 1: by step 2 some s₀ ∈ J has |x₀ − s₀| ≤ 5r_{s₀}, so θ_{s₀}(x₀) = 1, and every other term of the finite sum is ≥ 0.

9. The family and verification. Let ι be the type of elements of J (the subtype {s // s ∈ J} of ℝⁿ). For s ∈ J put φ_s(x) := θ_s(x)/Σ(x) and p_s := a_s, and let C := 3 and M := 30ΛN(N + 1). Clearly C ≥ 0 and M ≥ 0.
(P1) p_s = a_s ∈ A.
(P2) Let x ∈ U. θ_s and Σ are C^∞ at x and Σ(x) ≥ 1 ≠ 0, so φ_s = θ_s/Σ is C^∞, in particular C¹, at x.
(P3) For x ∈ U, θ_s(x) ≥ 0 and Σ(x) ≥ 1 > 0, so φ_s(x) ≥ 0.
(P4) For x₀ ∈ U take the finite set J'(x₀) (step 5) and V := B(x₀, r(x₀)), a neighbourhood of x₀ because r(x₀) > 0. For s ∉ J'(x₀) and y ∈ V, (7b) gives θ_s(y) = 0, hence φ_s(y) = 0.
(P5) For x ∈ U, (7b) with x₀ := x shows that s ↦ θ_s(x) and s ↦ φ_s(x) are supported in the finite set J'(x); hence Σᶠ_s φ_s(x) = Σ_{s∈J'(x)} θ_s(x)/Σ(x) = Σ(x)/Σ(x) = 1.
(P6) If x ∈ U and φ_s(x) ≠ 0, then θ_s(x) ≠ 0, so |x − s| < 9r_s < 10r_s, i.e. s ∈ J(x), and (F4) gives |x − p_s| < 3d(x) = C·d(x).
(P7) Let x ∈ U with d(x) ≤ 1, so r(x) = d(x)/20. If s ∉ J(x), then θ_s, hence φ_s, vanishes on B(x, r_s) by (7a), so Dφ_s(x) = 0. If s ∈ J(x), the quotient rule gives Dφ_s(x) = Dθ_s(x)/Σ(x) − θ_s(x)·DΣ(x)/Σ(x)², and with Σ(x) ≥ 1, 0 ≤ θ_s(x) ≤ 1, ‖Dθ_s(x)‖ ≤ Λ/r_s ≤ (3/2)Λ/r(x) and step 8, ‖Dφ_s(x)‖ ≤ ‖Dθ_s(x)‖ + ‖DΣ(x)‖ ≤ (3/2)Λ(N + 1)/r(x). Therefore s ↦ ‖Dφ_s(x)‖ is supported in the finite set J(x) and Σᶠ_s ‖Dφ_s(x)‖ = Σ_{s∈J(x)} ‖Dφ_s(x)‖ ≤ N·(3/2)Λ(N + 1)/r(x) = 30ΛN(N + 1)/d(x) = M/d(x).
This proves (P1)-(P7). ∎

Remarks for formalization. (i) Finite sums: finsum_eq_sum_of_support_subset; derivative of a sum that is locally a finite sum: Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq and fderiv_fun_sum (or HasFDerivAt.sum); ContDiffAt ℝ ∞ implies ContDiffAt ℝ 1 by ContDiffAt.of_le. (ii) The constants are immaterial: any construction giving (P1)-(P7) with some C, M ≥ 0 suffices. The pinned SimonGMT sources Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter02/WhitneyCover.lean, WhitneyPartition.lean, the nearest-anchor section of WhitneyJet.lean and the anchor lemma WhitneyBallCover.dist_near_anchor_le of WhitneyExtension.lean implement this construction with r = min{1,d}/100, enlargement 4 and bump radii 4 < 8 (exists_whitneyBallCover, whitneyWeight_contDiffAt, whitneyWeight_nonneg, whitneyWeight_eq_zero_of_notMem_nearFinset, sum_whitneyWeight_near, WhitneyBallCover.dist_near_anchor_le giving C = 2, exists_sum_norm_fderiv_whitneyWeight_bound giving M = 100·M₀ since whitneyRadius = d/100 when d ≤ 1). The prebuilt .olean files of those Whitney modules in the shared package tree are stale for Lake (lake build --no-build reports WhitneyCover and WhitneyJet as needing a rebuild), so do not import them from the submission; port their source into chapter-local modules (dropping the module/public keywords), which compiles with the pinned toolchain.
proof_key_steps: Scale r = min{1, d}/20 on U = ℝⁿ∖A; the Vitali lemma (τ = 5) selects pairwise disjoint balls B̄(s, r_s), s ∈ J, whose 5-fold enlargements cover U.

Geometry of the cover: comparable radii (F1), uniform overlap bound #J(x) ≤ N (F2), local finiteness of the 10-fold balls (F3), and nearest-point anchors a_s ∈ A with |x − a_s| < 3d(x) for s ∈ J(x) (F4).
Rescaled bumps θ_s = θ((· − s)/r_s) with ‖Dθ_s‖ ≤ Λ/r_s that vanish off B(s, 9r_s); their locally finite sum Σ is smooth on U with Σ ≥ 1 and ‖DΣ‖ ≤ (3/2)NΛ/r.
Set φ_s = θ_s/Σ, p_s = a_s, C = 3, M = 30ΛN(N+1), and verify (P1)-(P7) using the vanishing properties, the quotient rule and r = d/20 when d ≤ 1.

subproblems.title: C¹ gluing of a Whitney jet by a Whitney partition of unity
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), A ⊆ ℝⁿ closed, h : ℝⁿ → ℝ, and ν : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ continuous on A, and assume (W): for every compact K ⊆ A and every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 with |h(y) − h(x) − ⟨ν(x), y − x⟩| ≤ ε|y − x| for all x ∈ K and y ∈ A with 0 < |y − x| < δ. Let ι be a type, φ_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ and p_i ∈ ℝⁿ (i ∈ ι), and C ≥ 0, M ≥ 0 reals such that, with d(x) := dist(x, A): (P1) p_i ∈ A for all i; (P2) every φ_i is C¹ at every x ∉ A; (P3) φ_i(x) ≥ 0 for x ∉ A; (P4) every x ∉ A has a neighbourhood V and a finite s ⊆ ι with φ_i ≡ 0 on V for i ∉ s; (P5) Σᶠ_i φ_i(x) = 1 for x ∉ A; (P6) x ∉ A and φ_i(x) ≠ 0 imply |x − p_i| ≤ C·d(x); (P7) x ∉ A and d(x) ≤ 1 imply Σᶠ_i ‖Dφ_i(x)‖ ≤ M/d(x). If g : ℝⁿ → ℝ satisfies g(x) = h(x) for x ∈ A and g(x) = Σᶠ_i φ_i(x)(h(p_i) + ⟨ν(p_i), x − p_i⟩) for x ∉ A, then g is C¹ on ℝⁿ and Dg(x)v = ⟨ν(x), v⟩ for every x ∈ A and v ∈ ℝⁿ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Set (Rn n)) (h : Rn n → ℝ) (ν : Rn n → Rn n) (ι : Type) (φ : ι → Rn n → ℝ) (p : ι → Rn n) (C M : ℝ) (g : Rn n → ℝ), IsClosed A → ContinuousOn ν A → (∀ K ⊆ A, IsCompact K → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ A, 0 < ‖y - x‖ → ‖y - x‖ < δ → |h y - h x - inner ℝ (ν x) (y - x)| ≤ ε * ‖y - x‖) → 0 ≤ C → 0 ≤ M → (∀ i, p i ∈ A) → (∀ i, ∀ x ∉ A, ContDiffAt ℝ 1 (φ i) x) → (∀ i, ∀ x ∉ A, 0 ≤ φ i x) → (∀ x ∉ A, ∃ s : Finset ι, ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 x, ∀ i ∉ s, ∀ y ∈ V, φ i y = 0) → (∀ x ∉ A, ∑ᶠ i, φ i x = 1) → (∀ i, ∀ x ∉ A, φ i x ≠ 0 → ‖x - p i‖ ≤ C * Metric.infDist x A) → (∀ x ∉ A, Metric.infDist x A ≤ 1 → ∑ᶠ i, ‖fderiv ℝ (φ i) x‖ ≤ M / Metric.infDist x A) → (∀ x ∈ A, g x = h x) → (∀ x ∉ A, g x = ∑ᶠ i, φ i x * (h (p i) + inner ℝ (ν (p i)) (x - p i))) → ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ ∀ x ∈ A, ∀ v, fderiv ℝ g x v = inner ℝ (ν x) v
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: this is steps 4-6 of the parent-supplied proof of WhitneyExtension (Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6, proof supplied after [EG92], Whitney's extension theorem), extracted for an abstract Whitney partition of unity: the parent's constants 3 (anchor bound (F4)) and 20NC₁ (derivative bound) become the parameters C and M, and the parent's modulus ω of ν on K_a is replaced by continuity of ν at the base point (ν(p) − ν(q) = (ν(p) − ν(a)) − (ν(q) − ν(a))). Notation: ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), |·| the Euclidean norm, ‖·‖ the operator norm of a linear functional, U := ℝⁿ∖A, d(x) := Metric.infDist x A, L_y := ⟨ν(y), ·⟩ (so ‖L_y − L_z‖ = |ν(y) − ν(z)|), and P_i(y) := h(p_i) + ⟨ν(p_i), y − p_i⟩, an affine function with derivative L_{p_i} at every point.

Hypotheses. A is closed, ν is continuous on A, and (W): for every compact K ⊆ A and ε > 0 there is δ > 0 with |h(y) − h(x) − ⟨ν(x), y − x⟩| ≤ ε|y − x| for all x ∈ K, y ∈ A with 0 < |y − x| < δ. The family (φ_i, p_i)_{i∈ι} and the constants C ≥ 0, M ≥ 0 satisfy (P1) p_i ∈ A; (P2) φ_i is C¹ at every x ∈ U; (P3) φ_i ≥ 0 on U; (P4) every x ∈ U has a neighbourhood V and a finite s ⊆ ι with φ_i ≡ 0 on V for i ∉ s; (P5) Σᶠ_i φ_i(x) = 1 on U; (P6) x ∈ U, φ_i(x) ≠ 0 ⇒ |x − p_i| ≤ C·d(x); (P7) x ∈ U, d(x) ≤ 1 ⇒ Σᶠ_i ‖Dφ_i(x)‖ ≤ M/d(x). Finally g = h on A and g(x) = Σᶠ_i φ_i(x)P_i(x) for x ∈ U. Claim: g is C¹ and Dg(x)v = ⟨ν(x), v⟩ for x ∈ A, v ∈ ℝⁿ. (Continuity of h on A is not needed.)

Proof.

0. Two elementary facts.
(E1) For all a, b, y ∈ ℝⁿ: h(b) + ⟨ν(b), y − b⟩ − (h(a) + ⟨ν(a), y − a⟩) = [h(b) − h(a) − ⟨ν(a), b − a⟩] + ⟨ν(b) − ν(a), y − b⟩, because ⟨ν(a), y − a⟩ = ⟨ν(a), y − b⟩ + ⟨ν(a), b − a⟩.
(E2) d(x) ≤ |x − a| for every a ∈ A (infDist_le_dist_of_mem). If A ≠ ∅, then d(x) > 0 for every x ∈ U (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos). If A = ∅, then U = ℝⁿ, step 1 shows that g is C¹ at every point and the second conclusion is vacuous; steps 2-4 fix a point a ∈ A, so there A ≠ ∅.

1. Local structure on U. Fix x₀ ∈ U. By (P4) choose a finite s ⊆ ι and a neighbourhood V of x₀ with φ_i ≡ 0 on V for i ∉ s, and put W := V ∩ U, a neighbourhood of x₀ (U is open). For y ∈ W the functions i ↦ φ_i(y) and i ↦ φ_i(y)P_i(y) vanish outside s, so (finsum_eq_sum_of_support_subset, (P5))
(1a) g(y) = Σ_{i∈s} φ_i(y)P_i(y) and (1b) Σ_{i∈s} φ_i(y) = 1 for all y ∈ W.
(1c) G := Σ_{i∈s} φ_i·P_i is C¹ at x₀ (finite sum of products of the C¹-at-x₀ functions φ_i, by (P2), with affine functions) and g = G on W, so g is C¹ at x₀ (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). Hence g is differentiable at x₀, fderiv g is continuous at x₀ (ContDiffAt.continuousAt_fderiv), and by the product rule Dg(x₀) = Σ_{i∈s} [φ_i(x₀)L_{p_i} + P_i(x₀)Dφ_i(x₀)].
(1d) Σ_{i∈s} Dφ_i(x₀) = 0, by differentiating (1b): Σ_{i∈s} φ_i equals the constant 1 on the neighbourhood W.
(1e) Dφ_i(x₀) = 0 whenever i ∉ s (φ_i ≡ 0 on V) and whenever φ_i(x₀) = 0: in the latter case φ_i ≥ 0 on the open set U ∋ x₀ (P3), so x₀ is a local minimum of φ_i, which is differentiable at x₀ (P2), hence Dφ_i(x₀) = 0 (IsLocalMin.fderiv_eq_zero).
(1f) Let S := {i ∈ s : φ_i(x₀) ≠ 0}. By (P6), |x₀ − p_i| ≤ C·d(x₀) for i ∈ S. By (1b), Σ_{i∈S} φ_i(x₀) = 1 with all φ_i(x₀) ≥ 0. By (1e), i ↦ ‖Dφ_i(x₀)‖ is supported in s, so Σ_{i∈s} ‖Dφ_i(x₀)‖ = Σᶠ_i ‖Dφ_i(x₀)‖ ≤ M/d(x₀) whenever d(x₀) ≤ 1 (P7).
(1g) Consequently, for every a ∈ ℝⁿ and every pair of reals c, q: by (1a),(1b), g(x₀) − q = Σ_{i∈S} φ_i(x₀)(P_i(x₀) − q); and by (1c),(1b),(1d),(1e), Dg(x₀) − L_a = Σ_{i∈S} φ_i(x₀)(L_{p_i} − L_a) + Σ_{i∈S} (P_i(x₀) − c)Dφ_i(x₀).

2. Uniform estimates near a ∈ A. Fix a ∈ A and ε > 0. Let K := A ∩ B̄(a, 1); K is compact (closed and bounded in ℝⁿ), K ⊆ A and a ∈ K. By (W) choose δ₁ > 0 with |h(y) − h(x) − ⟨ν(x), y − x⟩| ≤ ε|y − x| for x ∈ K, y ∈ A, 0 < |y − x| < δ₁; this inequality holds trivially when y = x. By continuity of ν at a within A choose τ > 0 with |ν(y) − ν(a)| ≤ ε for y ∈ A, |y − a| < τ. Put ρ := min{1, δ₁, τ}/(C + 2) > 0; note (C + 1)ρ < min{1, δ₁, τ} and 2ρ ≤ min{1, δ₁, τ} because C ≥ 0. Let |x − a| < ρ. Then:
(2a) d(x) ≤ |x − a| < ρ ≤ 1/2 by (E2).
(2b) If x ∈ U and φ_i(x) ≠ 0, then |x − p_i| ≤ C·d(x) ≤ C|x − a| (P6) and |p_i − a| ≤ |p_i − x| + |x − a| ≤ (C + 1)|x − a| < min{1, δ₁, τ}; so p_i ∈ K (by (P1)), |ν(p_i) − ν(a)| ≤ ε and, by (W) with base point a ∈ K and y = p_i, |h(p_i) − h(a) − ⟨ν(a), p_i − a⟩| ≤ ε|p_i − a| ≤ ε(C + 1)|x − a|.

3. Differentiability on A. Fix a ∈ A; we show HasFDerivAt g L_a a. Let ε > 0 and take ρ as in step 2; let |x − a| < ρ. Recall g(a) = h(a).
- If x ∈ A: |g(x) − g(a) − L_a(x − a)| = |h(x) − h(a) − ⟨ν(a), x − a⟩| ≤ ε|x − a|, by (W) with base point a ∈ K and y = x (|x − a| < ρ < δ₁), trivially if x = a.
- If x ∈ U: apply (1g) at x₀ := x with q := h(a) + ⟨ν(a), x − a⟩. For i ∈ S, (E1) with b := p_i, y := x gives P_i(x) − q = [h(p_i) − h(a) − ⟨ν(a), p_i − a⟩] + ⟨ν(p_i) − ν(a), x − p_i⟩, whose absolute value is ≤ ε(C + 1)|x − a| + ε·C|x − a| = ε(2C + 1)|x − a| by (2b). As the weights φ_i(x), i ∈ S, are ≥ 0 with sum 1, |g(x) − g(a) − L_a(x − a)| ≤ ε(2C + 1)|x − a|.
So |g(x) − g(a) − L_a(x − a)| ≤ (2C + 1)ε|x − a| whenever |x − a| < ρ. Since ε > 0 is arbitrary and 2C + 1 is fixed, g(x) − g(a) − L_a(x − a) = o(|x − a|), i.e. HasFDerivAt g L_a a (HasFDerivAt.of_isLittleO with Asymptotics.IsLittleO.of_bound). In particular Dg(a)v = ⟨ν(a), v⟩ for all v.

4. Continuity of Dg at points of A. Fix a ∈ A and η > 0. Choose ε > 0 with ε(1 + (3C + 1)M) < η, and ρ as in step 2 for this ε. Let |x − a| < ρ.
- If x ∈ A: by step 3, Dg(x) − Dg(a) = L_x − L_a, of norm |ν(x) − ν(a)| ≤ ε < η, since |x − a| < ρ < τ.
- If x ∈ U: choose a* ∈ A with |x − a*| = d(x) (IsClosed.exists_infDist_eq_dist; ℝⁿ is proper). Then |a* − a| ≤ |a* − x| + |x − a| ≤ 2|x − a| < 2ρ ≤ min{1, δ₁, τ}, so a* ∈ K and |ν(a*) − ν(a)| ≤ ε. For i ∈ S (notation of (1f) at x₀ := x): by (2b), |ν(p_i) − ν(a)| ≤ ε, so |ν(p_i) − ν(a*)| ≤ 2ε; |x − p_i| ≤ C·d(x); and |p_i − a*| ≤ |p_i − x| + |x − a*| ≤ (C + 1)d(x) ≤ (C + 1)|x − a| < δ₁, so (W) with base point a* ∈ K and y = p_i gives |h(p_i) − h(a*) − ⟨ν(a*), p_i − a*⟩| ≤ ε|p_i − a*| ≤ ε(C + 1)d(x). With c := P*(x) := h(a*) + ⟨ν(a*), x − a*⟩, (E1) (with a := a*, b := p_i, y := x) yields |P_i(x) − c| ≤ ε(C + 1)d(x) + 2ε·C·d(x) = ε(3C + 1)d(x). Now (1g) at x₀ := x, (1f) and d(x) ≤ 1 (2a), d(x) > 0 give
‖Dg(x) − L_a‖ ≤ Σ_{i∈S} φ_i(x)|ν(p_i) − ν(a)| + Σ_{i∈S} |P_i(x) − c|·‖Dφ_i(x)‖ ≤ ε + ε(3C + 1)d(x)·Σ_{i∈s}‖Dφ_i(x)‖ ≤ ε + ε(3C + 1)d(x)·M/d(x) = ε(1 + (3C + 1)M) < η.
Since Dg(a) = L_a (step 3), ‖Dg(x) − Dg(a)‖ < η for all |x − a| < ρ; thus fderiv g is continuous at a.

5. Conclusion. g is differentiable at every point of U (1c) and of A (step 3), so g is differentiable on ℝⁿ; fderiv g is continuous at every point of U (1c) and of A (step 4), so fderiv g is continuous. By contDiff_one_iff_fderiv, g is C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 g). For x ∈ A and v ∈ ℝⁿ, step 3 gives fderiv ℝ g x v = L_x v = ⟨ν(x), v⟩. ∎

Remark for formalization. The pinned SimonGMT source Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter02/WhitneyExtension.lean (with WhitneyJet.lean) carries out the same estimates for its specific Whitney cover: whitneyAffine_sub_eq is (E1), whitneyExtension_sub_affine_eq_near_sum and whitneyExtension_fderiv_sub_eq_near_sum are (1g), HasWhitneyC1Compatibility.hasFDerivAt_whitneyExtension is step 3, continuousAt_fderiv_whitneyExtension is step 4 and contDiff_whitneyExtension is step 5; norm_sum_smul_le_of_convex_weights handles the convex combinations. Its proofs transfer to the abstract hypotheses (P1)-(P7) by replacing nearFinset with the finite set S = {i ∈ s : φ_i(x) ≠ 0} of (1f) (s from (P4)), after dropping the indices of s with φ_i(x) = 0 by (1e) (zero weight and zero derivative); the anchor bound (P6) is only available on S. That module has no prebuilt .olean in the shared package tree and its imported Whitney modules are stale for Lake, so port the source into chapter-local modules instead of importing it.
proof_key_steps: Locally on U (finite s from (P4)): g = Σ_{i∈s} φ_i P_i is C¹, Σ_{i∈s} φ_i = 1, Σ_{i∈s} Dφ_i = 0, and Dφ_i(x) = 0 wherever φ_i(x) = 0 (local minimum of a nonnegative function).
Near a ∈ A: (W) on the compact K = A ∩ B̄(a,1) and continuity of ν at a, with ρ = min{1,δ₁,τ}/(C+2), control every anchor p_i with φ_i(x) ≠ 0, since |p_i − a| ≤ (C+1)|x − a|.
First-order estimate |g(x) − g(a) − ⟨ν(a), x − a⟩| ≤ (2C+1)ε|x − a| for |x − a| < ρ, hence HasFDerivAt g ⟨ν(a),·⟩ a.
Derivative estimate on U via a nearest point a*: ‖Dg(x) − ⟨ν(a),·⟩‖ ≤ ε(1 + (3C+1)M); on A, ‖Dg(x) − Dg(a)‖ = |ν(x) − ν(a)| ≤ ε; hence fderiv g is continuous at a.
contDiff_one_iff_fderiv gives ContDiff ℝ 1 g, and fderiv ℝ g x v = ⟨ν(x), v⟩ for x ∈ A.
